newsitem.title: GREECE: Ecu/drachma capped below 310, fx forwards ease.
newsitem.headline: Ecu/drachma capped below 310, fx forwards ease.

text.p: Ecu/drachma opened at 310 and eased to 309.85/90 after the central bank checked $/drachma rates but light local ecu buying pushed it higher to 309.90/95, forex dealers said.
"It is quiet but there is tension," said a forex dealer at a foreign bank. "Ecu/drachma eased to 309.85/90 after the central bank checked $/drachma but it remains vulnerable."

The Bank of Greece had signalled to the market that it wanted ecu/drachma below 310 but forex outflows estimated at over $1.0 billion in the last couple of days cast their shadow on the market, dealers said.
"The central bank must have sold $1.0 billion or more at the fixing and its afternoon windows in the last couple of days to support the drachma," said a senior forex dealer at a foreign bank.
Mark/drachma showed signs of invigoration on ecu/mark softness and dollar/drachma was steadying above 282 on a robust $/mark, dealers said.

"It does not pay to be in currencies other than the $ especially if you are a U.S investor and forecast an even stronger dollar ahead," said another dealer. "What we have seen in Greece is position squaring driven by expectations of a stronger dollar."
He added that there was a speculative component in ecu/drachma moves but it was relatively small.
"These guys have made lots of money in the Czech crown but have lost lots of money in Thailand," he said. "So they are careful."

Depos were holding late Wednesday's high altitudes on tight liquidity conditions linked to the forex outflows and Tuesday's bond auction but forex forwards were easier, especially in two-month to six-month tenors, dealers said.
Bonds were holding late Wednesday levels and bond dealers said 95 was a strong price level for the 10-year bonds.
Greece allocated 82.5 billion drachmas each of five- and seven-year bonds with coupons of 9.2 percent and 8.9 percent respectively, and 132 billion drachmas of 8.8 percent, 10-year bonds on Tuesday.
It will also auction 150 billion drachmas of seven-year floating rate notes on July 29.
The mark was quoted at 156.95/00 from Wednesday's 156.990 fix, the dollar at 282.42/52 drachmas from 281.500 and the ecu at 309.84/94 from 309.92 drachmas.
